title: Hormones and Weight: Beyond Calories In, Calories Out

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: How do hormones like leptin, ghrelin, cortisol, and thyroid hormones influence body weight beyond simple calorie counting?
reader_intent: Understand the hormonal complexity of weight regulation to reduce self-blame and set realistic expectations.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands leptin resistance, ghrelin's rise after weight loss, cortisol's effect on fat storage, and thyroid's role, and knows these are testable via a healthcare provider.

claims.proposition: Leptin resistance can cause persistent hunger despite adequate or high fat stores.
claims.recommended_action: Standard endocrinology; article cites Endocrine Society/NIDDK/NIH generally rather than a specific leptin-resistance study, but this is a well-established, appropriately hedged mechanism claim.

claims.proposition: Ghrelin levels tend to increase with weight loss, contributing to increased hunger during and after dieting.
claims.recommended_action: Well-established and consistent with claim-biggestloser-metabolic-adaptation-residual's broader adaptive-response theme, though not directly citing Fothergill; general sourcing to Endocrine Society/NIH is adequate for this qualitative claim.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Set point theory directly builds on the ghrelin/leptin mechanisms introduced here.

disposition_reason: Well-hedged standard endocrinology with real organizational sourcing (Endocrine Society, NIDDK, American Thyroid Association, NIH, Harvard) matching the qualitative, non-specific-numeric claims actually made. No unsupported specific statistics. Only trivial editing needed.
